clue.text: Difficulty over reversing vehicle outside residential area

indicators.note: outside says the turned vehicle goes around the turned difficulty, enclosing it
reversing sits by vehicle, so that one word is read from right to left

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle

indicators.note: over follows difficulty and says that word is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: a rub is a difficulty, as in 'there's the rub'

explanation.surface: A driver struggles to back a large vehicle out of a housing estate.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate turnarounds: 'over' acts on the difficulty and 'reversing' on the vehicle; the turned vehicle is then split so its first two letters and last letter sit 'outside' the other piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A suburb is an outlying district where people live, a residential area beyond a city centre.

clue.text: Manoeuvres stones supporting beds of rock

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue means the stones sit beneath the beds of rock

parts.note: strata are layers or beds of rock
gems are precious stones

explanation.surface: Geology: stones holding up layers of rock in the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue a piece 'supporting' another is placed below it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stratagems are cunning schemes or manoeuvres devised to outwit someone.

clue.text: More conservative individual who squanders?

definitions.meaning: blue is the colour of the Conservative party, so more Tory is a comparative of blue
to blue money is old slang for squandering it, so one who does so

explanation.surface: Asking whether a more right-wing person is a spendthrift.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue is the British Conservative Party's colour; to blue money is to spend it recklessly.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain blue signals Conservative politics, so a person bluer is further to the right; the agent noun suits one who wastes money.

clue.text: Cylindrical pole or perch, so to speak

parts.note: the rod, pole and perch are all old names for the same unit of length
like is the filler word used informally, meaning so to speak

explanation.surface: Describing a round pole or a bird's perch, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: Pole, perch and rod are the same old unit of five and a half yards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shaped like a rod is long and round in section, so cylindrical.

clue.text: By no means the first writer's venue for hill-walking!

definitions.text: By no means the first writer's venue for hill-walking!

parts.words: By no means the first writer's venue for hill-walking
parts.note: read as the ninth pen's place, not pen number one's: a writing pen numbered nine, plus the possessive, gives the name of a range for walkers

explanation.surface: A remark that this upland walking area was hardly the first author's haunt.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue splits as PEN NINE'S: not the first pen (writer) but the ninth. The PENNINES are the hill range running down northern England, popular with walkers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pennine hills form a long upland chain in northern England, well known for hiking routes such as the Pennine Way.

clue.text: Wise European that's entertaining sailors

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the sailors are held within the other letters

parts.note: ie, id est, means that is
RN is the Royal Navy, the sailors

explanation.surface: A wise European who keeps sailors amused.
explanation.walkthrough: Ernie Wise was half of the British comedy double act Morecambe and Wise, so 'Wise' defines his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie Wise was the straight man of Morecambe and Wise, so Wise is his surname cueing the first name.

clue.text: Chat about one becoming less scruffy

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the chat goes round the one

parts.note: to natter is to chat
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Talking about someone who has smartened up.
explanation.definitionFit: Natty means smart and neat, so nattier is the comparative, the opposite of scruffier.

clue.text: Unsettling hour, being someone close

indicators.note: unsettling means disturbing, so the letters of hour and being are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unnerving hour spent with someone nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: A neighbour is a person living close by, literally someone close.

clue.text: Location that's a blot on the landscape, say

indicators.note: say tells us to take the word as spoken rather than as written

parts.note: an eyesore is called a sight, as in 'you look a sight'

explanation.surface: A place that spoils the scenery, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a location, the place where something stands or happens.

clue.text: Stress rate of progress accepted by each sibling

indicators.note: accepted by means taken in by, so the rate goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: mph, miles per hour, measures a rate of progress
sis is short for sister, a sibling

explanation.surface: Pressure from how fast each brother or sister is getting on.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphasis means special importance or stress placed on something.

clue.text: Sports club employee no good as milk deliverer

indicators.note: no in front of good says the good letter is dropped from the employee

parts.note: a groundsman looks after the pitch at a sports club

explanation.surface: A sports club worker who is useless at his second job delivering milk.
explanation.walkthrough: A roundsman is a British delivery worker who does a regular round, classically the milkman.
explanation.definitionFit: A roundsman makes deliveries on a fixed round, and the classic example is the milkman bringing bottles to doorsteps.

clue.text: It isn't commonly a corrupt condition

parts.note: in dialect or casual speech 'it' is shortened to 't, as in 'twas
ain't is the common, non-standard form of isn't

explanation.surface: A slangy claim that something is not a state of corruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commonly' signals informal speech, so 'It isn't' becomes 'T AIN'T, run together.
explanation.definitionFit: A taint is a trace of contamination or moral corruption, so it is a corrupt condition.

clue.text: The girl this duke abandoned out East is sweet

indicators.note: abandoned here means wild and unrestrained, so the letters are thrown into a new order
out tells us the letter for East is put out of the duke

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A duke deserts a girl somewhere in the Orient, which sounds rather sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes E from DUKE, leaving DUK; 'abandoned' then mixes THEGIRLTHISDUK into the confection's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Turkish delight is a cubed jelly confection dusted with sugar, a classic sweet.

clue.text: Superficially attractive bag lady?

parts.note: a bag is the catch or haul of game or fish
Penny is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A lady with an attractive handbag, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bag' is not a handbag but a haul, as a hunter's bag.
explanation.definitionFit: Catchpenny describes cheap, showy goods made to attract buyers, so superficially attractive.

clue.text: Sticky substance Maxim for example recalled

parts.note: the Maxim was an early machine gun, named after its inventor

indicators.note: recalled read as called back, so the short abbreviation is turned round

explanation.surface: A saying offered as an example of something sticky, remembered later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maxim' looks like a saying but is the Maxim machine gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunge is informal British slang for an unpleasant sticky or messy substance.

clue.text: Sailor run over in unsophisticated story

indicators.note: in means placed inside the unsophisticated word

parts.note: naive means unsophisticated

indicators.note: over here means turned over, so sailor and run are read backwards

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A simple tale of a sailor knocked down by a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns TAR plus R to RRAT, which goes into NAIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative is an account of events, that is, a story.

clue.text: Backing of old county theatre company by American star

indicators.note: backing means running in reverse, so the whole string of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: Avon was an English county abolished in 1996
rep is short for a repertory theatre company

explanation.surface: A theatre troupe from a former county gets the support of an American celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing of' turns AVONREPUS round. Avon was a short-lived English county around Bristol and Bath.
explanation.definitionFit: A supernova is a star that explodes and briefly blazes far brighter than normal.

clue.text: One leaving capital pinches food

indicators.note: leaving says the one departs from the capital city's name

parts.note: Paris is a capital city
I is the Roman numeral one
nips are small pinches

explanation.surface: A person leaving the city steals some food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinches' looks like stealing but means nips.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsnips are root vegetables, a kind of food.

clue.text: Inspector arrests girl beginning to ridicule preacher

indicators.note: arrests means holds, so the inspector's name wraps round the other letters

parts.note: Inspector Morse is the Oxford detective of the British novels and TV series
Ali is a girl's name

indicators.note: beginning to points to the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A police inspector detains a young woman who began mocking a preacher.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Morse is the fictional Oxford detective of British novels and television; 'arrests' means holds, so the girl and the first letter of 'ridicule' sit inside his name.
explanation.definitionFit: A moraliser lectures others on right and wrong, much as a preacher does.

clue.text: As one may be after convivial time in club lacking members?

definitions.text: As one may be after convivial time
definitions.meaning: very drunk after a sociable session at the bar
a club without legs, members being limbs

explanation.surface: A night at the club leaves a drinker unable to stand.
explanation.walkthrough: Legless is British slang for very drunk; 'members' are limbs, so the club lacks legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Legless is British slang for extremely drunk, and literally means without legs, the limbs a body has.

clue.text: Literary courtier dipping into hero's riches

indicators.note: dipping into says the answer sits inside the following words, spanning them

explanation.surface: A courtier in a story helps himself to a hero's wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: Osric is the foppish courtier in Shakespeare's Hamlet.
explanation.definitionFit: Osric is a courtier in Shakespeare's Hamlet, so a character from literature at court.

clue.text: Moor small pedalo finally after hotel trips

indicators.note: trips means stumbles, so the hotel letters fall into disorder
finally picks out the last letter of the words small and pedalo

explanation.surface: A small boat comes last after outings from the hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trips' turns HOTEL into OTHEL; 'finally' takes L and O from small and pedalo.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is Shakespeare's Moor of Venice, the title character of the tragedy.

clue.text: Like one who's mad, being taken unawares?

definitions.meaning: someone hopping mad is furious, and literally hopping means being on the hop

explanation.surface: A person caught off guard reacts with fury.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is playful: a person who is hopping mad could be said to be found on the hop.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means surprised while unprepared; whimsically it also describes someone found hopping, as when hopping mad.

clue.text: Obsession revealed in article

definitions.meaning: having a ... about something means being obsessed by it
an article is an object or item

explanation.surface: An obsession appears in a newspaper article.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing is an object or article, and also an obsession, as in having a thing about cats.

clue.text: Wind up composer, having change of heart

indicators.note: change of heart says the central letter of the composer's name is swapped

parts.note: Gustav Holst composed The Planets

explanation.surface: Teasing a composer who changes his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle L of HOLST becomes I.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoist is to raise or wind up, as with a winch.

clue.text: Artist endlessly climbing way over the hill

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means rising, so the letters are read upwards
endlessly means the last letter of the artist is dropped

parts.note: Degas was the French Impressionist painter

explanation.surface: A painter clambers a long way up a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts DEGAS to DEGA; 'climbing' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Aged means very old, and someone way over the hill is long past their prime.

clue.text: Brotherhood mostly showing English cunning

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the brotherhood word

parts.note: a guild is a brotherhood of craftsmen or merchants

explanation.surface: A fraternity largely displays English craftiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Guile is crafty deceit, a synonym for cunning used as a noun.

clue.text: Force to change oil in sump

indicators.note: to change says the letters of oil in sump are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice that you must change the oil in your car's sump.
explanation.definitionFit: Impulsion is a driving force or impetus, the push that sets something moving.

clue.text: Line up mature assemblage for equestrian discipline

indicators.note: assemblage means putting together, so the two pieces are joined in order

parts.note: to dress ranks is to line soldiers up straight
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: Arranging mature components for a horse-riding event.
explanation.walkthrough: DRESS is the military sense: troops dress when they align their ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressage is the horse-riding discipline of precise trained movements, an Olympic equestrian event.

clue.text: Expensive business, investing money in filthy dwelling

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: investing money in means putting it inside, so the money letter goes into the dwelling

parts.note: a sty is a filthy dwelling, literally a pigsty
L stands for pound, the old librae sign for money

explanation.surface: A firm sinking cash into a squalid property is a pricey move.
explanation.walkthrough: L comes from the pound sign, so it can stand for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Costly is a direct synonym of expensive, describing something that costs a lot.
